mPqWstVnRjQ.summary: A two-hour Joe Rogan Experience conversation with mycologist Paul Stamets about fungi, mycelium, bioremediation and medicinal mushrooms. It touches on Lion's Mane, psilocybin and the many uses of fungi.
mPqWstVnRjQ.why: Commenters offer it as a fascinating, accessible introduction to the world of fungi whenever mushrooms or mycelium come up.

mw2z9lV3W1g.summary: In this TED talk, Lawrence Lessig argues that American politics is corrupted by Congress's dependence on funding from a tiny fraction of citizens. He uses rapid-fire visuals and calls for a bipartisan push to reclaim the Republic.
mw2z9lV3W1g.why: HN cites it repeatedly as the root-cause argument that money in politics must be fixed before other issues, and as background for his Mayday PAC.

mScpHTIi-kM.summary: Veritasium explores the Prisoner's Dilemma and Axelrod's tournaments, showing why tit-for-tat and forgiving strategies win in repeated games. It extends the ideas to cooperation in evolution and conflict.
mScpHTIi-kM.why: HN commenters reach for it constantly as an approachable explanation of why cooperation and reciprocity are rational strategies.

msVuCEs8Ydo.summary: PBS Space Time argues that the speed of light is better understood as the speed of causality, the universal limit on how fast cause and effect propagate. Light travels at that speed because it is massless, but the limit itself is a property of spacetime.
msVuCEs8Ydo.why: HN commenters send people to it whenever a thread confuses the speed of light with a light-specific limit, and several say it deepened their understanding of relativity.

m3svKOdZijA.summary: Brian Lonsdorf explains why Underscore.js falls short as a functional programming library, then introduces currying, composition and point-free style in JavaScript. He argues for data-last argument ordering.
m3svKOdZijA.why: A repeatedly recommended introduction to functional JavaScript that explains currying and why data should come last.

mD4L7xDNCmA.summary: Mike Hearn's talk at the 2012 London Bitcoin Conference on the future of Bitcoin, new applications and rebuilding the banking system. He covers lesser-known protocol features such as contracts, escrow and scripting.
mD4L7xDNCmA.why: Recommended as a great overview of what Bitcoin's protocol can do beyond simple payments, particularly contracts and smart property.

mII9NZ8MMVM.summary: A 30-minute animated film explaining how money, banking and the Federal Reserve work and arguing that the American economy is heading for collapse. It is opinionated and has a strong point of view.
mII9NZ8MMVM.why: Recommended as an accessible animated primer on banking and the Fed, usually with the caveat that it is biased and dated.

mbEfzuCLoAQ.summary: Wendover Productions explains why US passenger rail lags behind other countries. It covers freight companies owning most of the track, geography and population density, and the economics of competing with flying.
mbEfzuCLoAQ.why: HN recommends it as a short, solid walkthrough of why American trains are slow and limited, most notably because freight gets priority.

mbyG85GZ0PI.summary: The first lecture of Caltech's CS 156 Machine Learning course by Yaser Abu-Mostafa, introducing the learning problem and supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning. It is one of 18 lectures in the Learning from Data course.
mbyG85GZ0PI.why: Recommended repeatedly in 'where do I start with ML' threads as a clear, math-aware introduction.

mVVNJKv9esE.summary: Cheng Lou's react-europe 2016 talk lays out a mental framework for thinking about abstraction levels in JavaScript tooling, from Angular and Grunt to Webpack and React. It uses that framework to reason about the cost of abstractions and how to choose between competing solutions.
mVVNJKv9esE.why: HN points to it as thought-provoking material on the tradeoffs and costs of abstraction, especially in frontend tooling debates.

mZyvIHYn2zk.summary: A SXSW talk by W Watson that uses Lacanian psychoanalysis, with nods to Zizek, to critique popular programming languages. It argues that people choose and defend languages for emotional and ideological reasons rather than rational ones.
mZyvIHYn2zk.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining and eye-opening look at the irrational psychology behind language preferences, though some note it is not scientifically precise.

modXC5IWTJI.summary: Jeff Dean of Google describes his experiences building Google's systems and how its infrastructure evolved over time. The Stanford talk covers search, scaling tipping points and lessons from building large-scale software.
modXC5IWTJI.why: HN recommends it as a classic look at systems engineering at Google, whose fundamentals have held up well despite its 2010 date.

m64SWl9bfvk.summary: Jon Moore's Strange Loop 2017 talk argues that rate limiting is the wrong tool for protecting services from noisy clients. He proposes concurrency-based capacity management and quotas instead.
m64SWl9bfvk.why: HN engineers recommend it for its core insight that limiting concurrency naturally yields request-rate limits, and for its link to queueing theory.

mOtKD7ml0NU.summary: Edwin Brady presents Idris 2, a rewrite of the Idris dependently typed language, and shows type-driven development in practice. The demos show the compiler filling in whole functions from their types.
mOtKD7ml0NU.why: HN points to it as a good introduction to Idris 2 and a striking demonstration of what dependent types enable.

mdKst8zeh-U.summary: An ESOTERICA episode tracing Yahweh from a warrior-storm god near Mt Seir to the god of the Israelites in the Judean highlands. It examines how Yahwism absorbed and contended with Canaanite religion.
mdKst8zeh-U.why: HN users recommend it as an impressively well-sourced, academic look at the origins of the Abrahamic religions.

mwrA5IRGpfU.summary: Isaac Freund, author of the River Wayland compositor, talks about writing a Wayland compositor in Zig. He covers why he chose Zig over C and Rust and how Zig can wrap a hairy C library.
mwrA5IRGpfU.why: HN recommends it as a phenomenal talk on Zig's C interop and on choosing between C, Rust and Zig for systems work.

m7PVZixO35c.summary: Matthias Wandel tests old and new code on a range of PCs, including a new mini PC, to measure how much faster modern hardware really is. He also shows optimization techniques such as branchless code, with benchmark programs on GitHub.
m7PVZixO35c.why: Used as evidence that CPU speed for branchy, dependent code has improved only modestly in 15-20 years, so software optimization matters.

meHYBhcpdvQ.summary: FortNine explains the economics of the dealership model, arguing that dealers absorb inventory risk and help manufacturers' finances. It looks at whether cars and motorcycles could be sold more cheaply without them.
meHYBhcpdvQ.why: Offered as a well-researched counterpoint in threads complaining about car dealerships and direct sales.

mhBpI13dxkI.summary: Karl Fogel's 2006 Google Tech Talk traces copyright from a 16th-century English censorship law to a distribution monopoly. It then surveys alternative economic bases for creation and distribution.
mhBpI13dxkI.why: HN uses it as the go-to history of copyright, arguing it was a gatekeeping tool and that creators don't need it.

mht-1c4wc0Q.summary: PBS Space Time explains what happens as you approach and cross a black hole's event horizon, using Penrose diagrams and light cones as the tool for understanding spacetime there.
mht-1c4wc0Q.why: Commenters call it a short, clean, visual explanation of the infalling-particle question and of Penrose diagrams.

mn4L_aJ1rV4.summary: Essential Craftsman announces the start of a spec house build on a scenic lot, kicking off a long series. The channel covers every step of building a house from the viewpoint of a general contractor.
mn4L_aJ1rV4.why: HN users recommend the Spec House series as a free, extremely detailed education in how a house is actually built.

msN87y-iEx0.summary: Richard Feynman, in a clip from the BBC series Fun to Imagine, takes on the puzzle of why mirrors seem to swap left and right but not top and bottom.
msN87y-iEx0.why: Cited as the best explanation of mirror reversal.

mvmuCPvRoWQ.summary: 3Blue1Brown builds intuition for Euler's formula, e^(pi i) = -1, using the core ideas of group theory. It treats exponentiation geometrically as rotation and scaling instead of repeated multiplication.
mvmuCPvRoWQ.why: Recommended as a mind-opening, visual explanation of why Euler's formula is true.

m05abdGSOxY.summary: Mark Handley of UCL explains, with simulation visualizations, how early Starlink satellites without inter-satellite links could still give low-latency wide-area communication by hopping via ground relays. He shows it can beat fibre on many long paths.
m05abdGSOxY.why: Cited in Starlink latency debates as a clear visual analysis showing sub-100ms latency is plausible even without inter-satellite links.

mHtdZgou0qU.summary: A 2009 Google Tech Talk by Nicholas Zakas on the hidden performance pitfalls of JavaScript. It covers what is fast and slow in the language and how to avoid common bottlenecks.
mHtdZgou0qU.why: Recommended as a classic JavaScript performance talk whose fundamentals about reflow and efficient code still apply.

mSB71jNq-yQ.summary: A short BBC Earth clip from David Attenborough's Life of Birds showing a lyrebird imitating sounds, including a chainsaw and camera shutter, so accurately it is hard to tell from the real thing.
mSB71jNq-yQ.why: Shared whenever birds mimic sounds come up, as a mind-blowing example of vocal mimicry.

muCPjK4nGY4.summary: A player piano is made to reproduce human speech, here reciting a European Environmental Criminal Court proclamation in German at the 2009 World Venice Forum. This upload adds subtitles so the words become understandable.
muCPjK4nGY4.why: HN recommends it as the canonical talking-piano example, uncanny and impressive once you read the captions.

m1lhGqNCZlA.summary: A DEF CON 24 talk on how a cyber mercenary group could forge identities and create the conditions for overthrowing a government. It is entertainingly outlandish and includes a drone-mounted saw for cutting power lines.
m1lhGqNCZlA.why: HN recommends it as an amazing, entertaining talk and cites it in threads on power-line sabotage and coup tactics.

mPZn4x3uOac.summary: Jacob Collier layers ten vocal parts to arrange and perform Harold Darke's carol "In the Bleak Midwinter", with inventive harmony and tuning.
mPZn4x3uOac.why: Recommended as a showcase of Collier's harmonic and microtonal skill.

mPn2AdMH7UQ.summary: A Numberphile interview with Donald Knuth about how he came to write the first book on surreal numbers after a lunch with John Conway. He tells the story casually in about 14 minutes.
mPn2AdMH7UQ.why: Recommended as a short, charming introduction to surreal numbers and to how Knuth wrote his book in under a week.

mSgXWpvQEHE.summary: Steven G. Johnson, MIT professor and FFTW co-author, gives a JuliaCon 2019 keynote on metaprogramming and staged programming in Julia, showing how it enables high-performance numerical code and when not to use macros.
mSgXWpvQEHE.why: Cited for showing how Julia's metaprogramming can beat C and Fortran, along with sound advice not to overuse it.

mUcUy7SqdS0.summary: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science shows how to make small batches of specialty glass with minimal equipment, including designing and making photochromic glass. He covers ingredients, melting and the challenges involved.
mUcUy7SqdS0.why: Recommended as a hands-on introduction to glass melting and chemistry and to Krasnow's channel.

mb3uK-_QkOo.summary: Brandon Sanderson's keynote on AI-generated art, arguing that the artistic process and the journey matter more than the finished product. He explains why he rebels against generative AI in creative work.
mb3uK-_QkOo.why: HN commenters share it as an eloquent argument that AI output is not art, and as a companion to worries about losing deep thinking.

meiU6TxysCg.summary: A short excerpt from Frans de Waal's TED talk showing a capuchin monkey fairness experiment in which two monkeys are paid unequally, one with cucumber and one with grapes. The shortchanged monkey reacts angrily.
meiU6TxysCg.why: HN uses it again and again as shorthand for the idea that resentment of unfair pay and inequality is built into primates, including us.

mmfjM-SGlGs.summary: Ted Nelson, the originator of hypertext and Project Xanadu, gives a personal account at age 80 of his ideals, his career, and how a poor career plan led to discoveries and adventures. It works as an alternative history of personal computing and hypertext.
mmfjM-SGlGs.why: HN people point to it as Nelson's candid, first-person overview of his life, Xanadu's failure, and the lessons he drew, a historical record from the man himself.

mpbeOCKZFfQ.summary: A Channel 4 News undercover investigation in which Cambridge Analytica executives are filmed discussing bribes, honeypots, fake identities and manipulating elections around the world.
mpbeOCKZFfQ.why: HN points to it as the primary evidence of what Cambridge Analytica was willing to do, especially in Facebook data scandal threads.

mOJlg8g8_yw.summary: Summoning Salt's roughly two-hour documentary traces the history of Tetris world records, from early play through the modern competitive scene. It is a long, well-researched narrative about the players and techniques that pushed the records.
mOJlg8g8_yw.why: HN recommends it as a thorough, well-researched history, and one commenter finds such videos more exhaustive than Wikipedia's sourced articles.

mXVGIb3bzHI.summary: Veritasium's Derek Muller spends an hour in a silent, dark anechoic chamber at BYU to test the claim that 45 minutes is the most anyone can bear. He reports on his experience and other people's reactions.
mXVGIb3bzHI.why: HN links it in threads about silence and quiet rooms, as a good first-hand look at the anechoic chamber that debunks the madness myth.

macM_MtS_w4.summary: A Computerphile video in which Mark Jago of the University of Nottingham explains Turing's halting problem and how it led to the blueprint for the modern computer.
macM_MtS_w4.why: Offered as a short, clear explanation of the halting problem and its link to decidability.

mceaM2_zQd8.summary: Matt Parker on Numberphile explains the strange properties of spheres in higher dimensions, such as how they poke out of their bounding boxes. It uses Pythagoras to build intuition for 4D and beyond.
mceaM2_zQd8.why: Recommended whenever the counterintuitive geometry of high-dimensional spheres comes up, including in vector embedding discussions.

mhJRzQsLZGg.summary: NASASpaceflight's 24/7 live stream from SpaceX's Starbase in Boca Chica, Texas, showing Starship and Super Heavy development, testing and launches.
mhJRzQsLZGg.why: Linked during Starship launches and testing as a live view that needs no login and shows the rockets actually being built.

msZ_E-4GFs8.summary: Matt Risinger demonstrates a blower door test on a house, using a fan to measure air leakage and find where air gets in and out. It shows how the test reveals the quality of the build.
msZ_E-4GFs8.why: HN recommends it as a good look at how blower door tests measure a home's energy efficiency and expose cut corners.

mzJmTCYmo9g.summary: John Bird and John Fortune satirize the investment banking mindset in a mock interview about the subprime mortgage crisis. The sketch lampoons structured credit products and the banks' reassurances shortly before the crash.
mzJmTCYmo9g.why: HN points to it as a funny but accurate send-up of banker thinking, noting that comedians grasped the crisis before Lehman collapsed.

mH0oCDa74tE.summary: 3Blue1Brown introduces group theory and abstract groups, then builds toward classification of finite simple groups and the enormous Monster group with its 196,883 dimensions.
mH0oCDa74tE.why: Mentioned as a favorite 3Blue1Brown video and a related watch in threads about deep mathematical structure.

mfv0V1SxbNA.summary: Linus Tech Tips builds a Linux PC together with Linus Torvalds, who talks through parts selection, kernel development and some of his side projects. The conversation also touches on AI in kernel work.
mfv0V1SxbNA.why: HN mines it for Torvalds's opinions, such as ECC RAM, AI hype, and his desktop setup, and as a rare long informal interview.

m1kHsd3Ocxc.summary: Munro Live's team breaks down the thermal management system of the Ford Mustang Mach-E and compares it with the Tesla Model Y. They look at parts count, coolant loops and heating approaches.
m1kHsd3Ocxc.why: Cited as engineering evidence that Tesla's integrated thermal design is far simpler than Ford's, in EV and quality debates.

m7_WDzPyoqU.summary: A More Perfect Union report from a small Texas town next to a large Bitcoin mining facility, where residents describe constant noise and health problems. It looks at the political and corporate power behind the facility.
m7_WDzPyoqU.why: Linked in crypto-mining threads for its picture of what nearby residents endure, though some commenters treat it as a case of corporations overriding locals.

mCSUmwP02T8.summary: Tom Scott visits the Strid at Bolton Abbey in Yorkshire, a deceptively narrow stretch of river with dangerous currents. He covers its reputation and the 12th-century legend of the Boy of Egremont.
mCSUmwP02T8.why: HN links it as the original, interesting video behind the 'deadliest river' stories and as an extreme river example.

mGQLXRTl3Z0.summary: A full performance by cellist Mischa Maisky of Bach's Cello Suite No. 1 in G, from a 1993 Unitel recording, with all six movements.
mGQLXRTl3Z0.why: Offered as a well-known, accessible example of Bach's appeal.

mLEOZO1GwVc.summary: A 24-minute interview with Edsger Dijkstra, the Dutch computer scientist, including his views on writing programs by hand and keeping errors out of them. It is part of a longer Dutch TV interview.
mLEOZO1GwVc.why: Shared as a primary source for Dijkstra's views, such as his approach to writing code on paper.

mSFHKAvTGNk.summary: A tool-assisted run of Brain Age by TASBot, shown at Awesome Games Done Quick 2016. The bot gives deliberately deranged answers while exploiting the game's error-prone recognition.
mSFHKAvTGNk.why: HN points to it as a funny, fun-to-watch example of what TAS can do to a game's input handling.

mZBwsm6B280.summary: Numberphile interviews Grant Sanderson of 3blue1brown about Bertrand's paradox, where different reasonable ways of picking a random chord of a circle give different probabilities.
mZBwsm6B280.why: Cited in threads on random sampling as a clear illustration of how reasonable-sounding random choices can give biased results.

makaJpLvbow.summary: Researchers from the Artificial Life Lab Graz introduce the Primordial Particle System, where a simple motion law for self-propelled particles produces cell-like structures that self-reproduce and show life cycles.
makaJpLvbow.why: Shared as an example of simple rules yielding complex emergent, life-like behavior, alongside Game of Life and particle simulators.

mbdXeRBbgDM.summary: Christian Schafmeister presents lessons from six years of implementing Clasp, a Common Lisp compiler using LLVM as its backend that interoperates with C++. He explains handling a dynamic, memory-managed language on LLVM.
mbdXeRBbgDM.why: Mostly cited by the author himself as the introduction to Clasp and Cando, and recommended to those wanting Lisp with C++ library interop.

mf5otGNbkuc.summary: Neuroscientist Beau Lotto runs the audience through color and pattern illusions to show that perception is shaped by context and evolutionary history rather than being a direct readout of the world. The talk is playful and hands-on, and it argues that the brain interprets ambiguous signals.
mf5otGNbkuc.why: HN commenters use it as a fun, accessible demonstration that color perception depends on surrounding patterns and that what we see differs from what the eyes register.

mj5IV23g-fE.summary: A three-minute rant by Harlan Ellison, excerpted from the documentary Dreams with Sharp Teeth, on why creative professionals should always be paid for their work rather than work for free or 'exposure'.
mj5IV23g-fE.why: The standard link whenever someone asks creatives to work unpaid or for publicity.

mu-tJc-BgaI.summary: A short demo shows how to use the Tesla Model 3's mechanical emergency door release on the front doors as a backup to the electronic release. It notes an on-screen warning that frequent use could damage the door seals.
mu-tJc-BgaI.why: HN cites it in threads about Teslas trapping occupants to show how the manual release is located and used.

mvrE2ZGe-rs.summary: Samuel Falvo II live-codes a text preprocessor and blog engine in Forth over about an hour. It shows Forth's dictionary being snapshotted and restored in place of mutation, and how a small Forth system gets real work done.
mvrE2ZGe-rs.why: Cited as a concrete look at Forth in action, including its snapshot/restore dictionary model.

mxDSiwqM2nw.summary: An extended Fifth Estate interview with Pierre Sprey, designer of the A-10 and a key figure behind the F-16, arguing the F-35 is an over-engineered, expensive failure.
mxDSiwqM2nw.why: Posted in F-35 threads as an insider's critique from a legendary aircraft designer.

m4OvQIGDg4I.summary: A one-minute clip from the film Office Space in which consultants ask an employee what he does here. It is a widely shared workplace comedy moment.
m4OvQIGDg4I.why: Used purely as a joke reply when threads discuss pointless roles, management or architects.

m4yVlPqeZwo.summary: Barack Obama, then a presidential candidate, presents his innovation agenda at Google and takes questions from Eric Schmidt and employees in November 2007.
m4yVlPqeZwo.why: Referenced for his answers on technology policy and the famous bubble sort question, and for comparing politics then and later.

m8Mc-38C88g.summary: A Margin Call clip in which Will Emerson tries to persuade Eric Dale to return to the firm, and Dale recounts calculating the lifetimes saved by a bridge he helped build.
m8Mc-38C88g.why: HN cites the scene when discussing small efficiency gains multiplied across many users, such as faster boot or load times.

m9-cNNYb1Ik.summary: A short NOVA excerpt in which David Pogue abuses a Tufts-developed battery by cutting and damaging it, and it keeps working without catching fire. It comes from the documentary 'Search for the Super Battery'.
m9-cNNYb1Ik.why: Cited repeatedly as a quick visual demonstration that solid-state or polymer batteries can survive abuse without igniting.

mArrNRWQEso.summary: A TED2014 interview in which Charlie Rose talks with Google CEO Larry Page about the company's long-term vision, including balloons for internet access and the DeepMind acquisition. Page also discusses data sharing and privacy.
mArrNRWQEso.why: Cited for specific Larry Page statements, such as on sharing medical data for research and personalized search being a hard problem.

mJHvSp9AKYg.summary: The Good Will Hunting scene in which Will explains to NSA recruiters why he would not work for them. It is a monologue on the ethics of national security work.
mJHvSp9AKYg.why: Brought up whenever NSA recruiting and hiring comes up, as a favorite scene capturing ethical objections to that work.

mJLr0KMsRAA.summary: Bloomberg shows Ross McNutt demonstrating his wide-area aerial surveillance system, following a shooting and the getaway car and piecing together a crime network.
mJLr0KMsRAA.why: Cited in surveillance threads as a demonstration of wide-area aerial tracking that existed years ago.

mKHY69AFstE.summary: A one-minute UK road safety advert showing a family car crash in which an unbelted rear passenger kills his mother in a head-on collision. It is a notoriously graphic public information film.
mKHY69AFstE.why: HN cites it as an example of fear-based public safety messaging that sticks in memory.

mKwL5G5HbGA.summary: Jamie Oliver shows school kids how chicken nuggets are made by blending skin and mechanically reclaimed meat, as part of his school lunch campaign. The kids react with disgust.
mKwL5G5HbGA.why: Mostly cited as an example of people still wanting nuggets after seeing how they are made, and sometimes criticized as misleading.

mOy8Xjaa_o8.summary: Tom Scott visits the US National Helium Reserve in Amarillo, Texas, and explains why headlines that the world is running out of helium are misleading. He covers the Federal Helium Program and its planned privatization.
mOy8Xjaa_o8.why: Cited to show that helium is not actually running out, and for background on the federal reserve.

mPna6D21Eqg.summary: A Curry On talk by Lars Bak, known for V8 and Dart, on building a secure and robust IoT development platform. It discusses language and VM design choices for small devices.
mPna6D21Eqg.why: Referenced mainly for Bak's firsthand account of why the Dart VM never shipped in Chrome and for his IoT language design points.

mPnx3zO3SDc.summary: A clip from Battlestar Galactica season 4 in which a character declares 'I'm a machine' and laments the limits of human senses.
mPnx3zO3SDc.why: HN uses it as a quoted joke in threads about human limitations versus machine perception.

mQT5aMa_7iI.summary: An animated Gabbard diagram of objects in low Earth orbit from 1959 to 2021, showing altitude over time. It highlights major debris-generating events and how low-altitude debris decays out of orbit.
mQT5aMa_7iI.why: HN uses it to illustrate orbital debris evolution and how altitude determines how fast debris decays.

mS5WYp5xmvI.summary: Thomas Sowell speaks at the Hoover Institution about economic and racial inequality and what he considers myths about poverty. He also recounts his early life and brief flirtation with Marxism.
mS5WYp5xmvI.why: Mostly cited as a source for Sowell's views on welfare, neighborhoods and his personal anecdotes.

mTABw0EyIWY.summary: Thunderf00t applies a simple energy mass balance to weight loss, showing how much exercise is needed to burn off extra calories compared with eating less. He concludes that cutting intake is the easier route and that hunger fades after the first week.
mTABw0EyIWY.why: HN cites it in arguments that exercise alone is an ineffective way to lose weight and that caloric deficit matters most.

mUmlv814aJo.summary: CGTN coverage of the 2026 Spring Festival Gala, in which humanoid robots perform synchronized martial arts routines alongside children.
mUmlv814aJo.why: Cited as a snapshot of Chinese humanoid robot capability, with some commenters doubting its authenticity.

mUqeBMP8nEg.summary: Former CIA Chief of Disguise Jonna Mendez reviews spy scenes from film and TV and explains how realistic they are, including disguise techniques and masks.
mUqeBMP8nEg.why: Referenced when discussing how real the disguise technology shown in spy movies is.

maAFcEU6atk.summary: Celery Man is a short Tim and Eric sketch in which Paul Rudd uses an absurd computer interface. It is a surreal comedy bit from their show.
maAFcEU6atk.why: HN mostly drops it as a joke or reference in threads about odd computer interfaces and AI tools, and one commenter points to this upload for its better quality.

me4BZBsHwZs.summary: A Louis C.K. bit from a Conan O'Brien appearance about airplane Wi-Fi and how quickly people feel entitled to new technology.
me4BZBsHwZs.why: HN invokes it as a joke whenever someone complains about a miraculous technology not working perfectly.

mfhAC2YiYHs.summary: Thunderf00t argues that the Pentagon's officially released 'UFO' videos have mundane explanations such as birds, parallax and sensor artifacts.
mfhAC2YiYHs.why: HN cites it as a debunking whenever Pentagon UFO footage is discussed.

mgAbfr42oI8.summary: A short hyperlapse of a 2019 Toyota Corolla using comma.ai's OpenPilot 0.6.3 to drive 100 miles with no intervention except for the windshield wipers.
mgAbfr42oI8.why: comma.ai repeatedly links it in its 'Who is hiring?' posts as a demo of its open source driving agent.

mr9kK0_7x08.summary: Marques Brownlee walks through Tesla's factory with Elon Musk, showing production lines for the Model S, X and 3.
mr9kK0_7x08.why: Mostly used as a reference clip, as a view of a modern factory or evidence in an argument, not as a recommendation.

msXtgTVMcuA.summary: A short clip of the Sprint anti-ballistic missile, which was launched from a silo and reached Mach 10 within seconds. Its nose and skin glow white hot from aerodynamic heating.
msXtgTVMcuA.why: HN links it as striking footage of how fast and heat-stressed hypersonic interceptors and ICBM re-entry vehicles are.

mty0RwkPmE8.summary: David Nolen reviews the first five years of ClojureScript, documenting its landmarks and looking ahead to the next five. It is a history-and-roadmap talk from the Clojure community.
mty0RwkPmE8.why: HN mentions it chiefly for a specific moment where Nolen credits Chris Granger and Light Table, and in a few hiring threads.

muPcHs-E4qc.summary: Not Just Bikes explains why Swiss trains are considered among the best in Europe and the world, covering frequency, connections and what riding them is like.
muPcHs-E4qc.why: HN cites it as an example of public transit that runs like clockwork and is convenient enough to rival cars.

mwdo17GT6sg.summary: A five-minute clip from The Big Short (2015) in which FrontPoint Partners confront Morgan Stanley risk assessors and an S&P ratings representative about inflated mortgage bond ratings.
mwdo17GT6sg.why: Used as a shorthand scene for conflicts of interest where auditors or raters are paid by the entities they judge.
